title: Workload fingerprinting & safe batch recommendation engine
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Problem: We need an automated, safe recommender that suggests continuous-batching and KV-cache configurations per workload to reduce per-token cost while preserving latency SLOs. Current manual tuning is slow, brittle, and doesn't generalize across shard topologies or varying sequence length distributions.

Scope: Build a batching recommendation engine that combines offline workload fingerprinting, light-weight online heuristics, and a controlled apply/rollback flow. The engine must: produce per-route recommendations (batch_size, max_latency_ms, batch_window_ms, continuous_batching_enabled, kv_cache_policy); estimate cost and latency delta; run dry-runs and canary applies; and automatically rollback on SLA regressions.

Goals:
- Reduce average per-token GPU cost for routed text-generation workloads by >= 12% on pilot routes without increasing p95 latency beyond SLO.
- Provide transparent reason strings for recommendations (e.g., "high prefix similarity -> enable prefix KV caching, lower window to 8ms").
- Safe rollout primitives: dry-run simulation, canary % rollout, automated rollback triggers, and manual override.

Non-goals: automated global rebalancing of reserved capacity, sample-level prompt rewriting, or cross-customer model changes (out of scope for pilot).
acceptance_criteria: Fingerprinting job collects per-route histograms for prompt length, continuation length, token-level latency, KV cache hit ratio, and request inter-arrival distribution over 7d
Offline estimator predicts cost and latency delta for a candidate batching config with mean absolute error < 8% vs measured dry-run
Heuristic engine emits recommendations categorized into: conservative / aggressive / experimental with reason text and expected cost delta
Apply flow supports dry-run (simulation) + canary rollout (1%, 5%, 25%) + automatic rollback if p95 latency increases > 10% or error rate increases > 0.5% within 30m
UI/Console card shows recommendation, confidence band, estimated savings, and a link to the dry-run report
Automation stores configs in versioned config store and tags each apply with rollout id for traceability
Integration tests that run on CI validate that a rollback trigger actually reverts active configs and surfaces an incident ticket
